title: I built this dark fantasy environment with 3D AI, Blender and UE5 in 72 hours
author: Delicious-Shower8401
selftext:
I built this dark fantasy environment in about 72 hours. I wanted to focus specifically on the **environment workflow** here: how I went from references and generated assets to a complete modular location inside Unreal Engine.

# Environment workflow

* **I started by breaking the scene into reusable assets** Instead of generating the entire environment as one piece, I separated it into stone walls, ruined sections, ground elements, pillars, props and architectural details. This made it much easier to control composition and reuse the same assets across the level.
* **Most of the 3D assets were generated with Tripo P2** This was probably the biggest time saver. I could generate individual architectural pieces from references and get relatively lightweight meshes with structured topology instead of starting every prop from a dense raw generation. For assets where I needed more control, I used P2's quad output and adjusted the target polycount depending on how important the object was in the scene. Tripo P2 supports native quad topology and configurable mesh density, which made the generated assets much easier to continue working with in Blender.
* **Large surfaces used tileable PBR materials** For the ground and large stone walls, unique textures would have been wasteful and would stretch quickly. I generated seamless stone materials separately and used tiled PBR textures instead.
* **The arena itself was assembled in Blender** I only needed to prepare a few good wall modules. Using **Array + Curve modifiers**, I could repeat and bend them into the circular arena, then manually destroy or modify sections where I wanted more variation.
* **Final materials and atmosphere were done in UE5** I rebuilt the important materials in Unreal, adjusted roughness and normal response, and then used fog, fire, lighting and weather to push the dark-fantasy atmosphere.

The part I like about **Tripo P2 for this kind of environment work is that the output doesn't feel like a dead-end AI mesh**. It can generate a low-poly, optimized asset with native quad topology and usable PBR materials, so I can bring it straight into Blender and keep working normally: reshape the silhouette, move loops, use modifiers, duplicate modules, change proportions or rebuild parts without fighting an unnecessarily dense mesh. P2 concentrates geometry where the shape actually needs detail and keeps simpler surfaces cleaner, which gives me much more flexibility during the post-process and makes it far more practical for a real game-environment pipeline.

replies.author: Delicious-Shower8401
replies.body: Either with Patina, which is made specifically for texture generation, or just with any image generator. I usually use Nano Banana 2 and prompt something like “generate a seamless 1K stone texture.” works pretty well for most materials!
